messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall: serving-runtime high error rate on continuous-batcher (us-west-2). Symptom: rising queue length, GPU OOMs, container restarts. Severity: P1. Please acknowledge.
ashok: on it. ACK. Looking at logs now.
maria: grabbing GPU metrics, is this the same host group that flapped yesterday?
ashok: yes, same pool (rbw-batcher-3). I'm seeing batch growth up to ~65k requests queued per node.
luis: logs show repeated CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED followed by container exit code 137. snippet:```
2026-03-14T22:35:08Z runtime ERROR cuda: CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED when allocating 6144MB
2026-03-14T22:35:08Z runtime INFO kill_container pid=2321 exit=137
```
jen: that exit pattern matches paging + VM OOM behaviour: kernel is swapping and then container gets oomkilled.
ashok: surface-level plan: (1) stop accepting new continuous batches to these nodes (route to fallback model), (2) scale down batch size and pause auto-batching, (3) restart affected nodes after clearing GPU memory. Who can run the route override?
tim_oncall: I can trigger a route override. What target? a smaller-quantized variant or CPU fallback?
maria: prefer quantized variant first to avoid huge latency jump for customers. route to model:gpt-small-q4 at priority=low.
luis: adding a short-term config change: reduce max_batch_tokens from 4096 -> 1024 and set batch_window_ms=15. Command:```
kubectl patch config continuous-batcher -n runtime --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/max_batch_tokens","value":1024},{"op":"replace","path":"/batch_window_ms","value":15}]'
```
ashok: executing patch now.
incident-bot: Route override applied by tim_oncall -> model: gpt-small-q4 (region: us-west-2).
jen: monitoring new traffic. early signs: p50 latency up ~20ms but p95 down from 6s -> 1.2s. Good.
maria: however we still see an instance repeatedly OOMing every ~45s. Node-level swap spikes at 96%. Need to isolate host.
luis: can we cordon and drain the node? kubectl drain will move non-critical pods; we need to ensure no in-flight long KV cache state is lost.
ashok: we have handoff mechanism for long-lived KV - use graceful drain flag. command I'm about to run:```
kubectl cordon rbw-batcher-3-7 && kubectl drain rbw-batcher-3-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=300
```
ashok: cordon succeeded. Drain started. Some pods failed to evict due to local storage.
maria: for pods that block, we can scale them down on their replica set with graceful termination. I'll patch replicaset to 0 for the runtime-worker on that node.
jen: customer impact so far: 3 customers reported increased latency and 1 reported failed requests (~0.2% of requests in us-west-2 window 22:33-22:41). I submitted a quick incident note to #customer-impact.
ashok: node drained eventually. restarting node service to clear potential driver leak. Command:```
sudo systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced && sudo docker restart --fix-gpu-driver
```
ashok: driver restart performed. Observed immediate drop in cuda allocation errors on that host.
maria: rolling restart for the rest of the pool with a 30s stagger. I'm sequencing 1/5 nodes now.
luis: small change request: enable kv-prefix-cache for the quantized model to reduce repeated prefix recomputation. Might lower per-token memory.
jen: accepted, make it a short-lived flag only for the next 12h.
incident-bot: Update: severity remains P1 until all nodes stable. Next automated check in 5m.
ashok: handoff: I need to go offline for childcare. @tim_oncall please take over post-22:45. I'll DM runbook notes.
tim_oncall: taking over. ACK. What's the next step if we see another OOM after restart?
maria: fallback to CPU model pool (model: gpt-mini-cpu) if OOMs persist after two restarts per node. Escalate to infra oncall if >2 nodes fail.
luis: also creating a temporary autoscaler cap to prevent too many batcher replicas scheduling on same GPU.```
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: batcher-hpa-temp
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: continuous-batcher
  minReplicas: 2
  maxReplicas: 8
  metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource:
      name: nvidia.com/gpu
      target:
        type: Utilization
        averageUtilization: 75
EOF
```
jen: created ticket INFRA-4521 to investigate driver memory leak hypothesis and kernel swap tuning. Assigning to @luis and @infra-oncall.
ashok: leaving notes in the thread about initial heap dumps and GPU coredumps saved to gs://redwood-incidents/1765432100/.
incident-bot: Automated post: saved logs and gcore dumps uploaded. link: https://artifacts.redwood/1765432100/
maria: after the routing + batch-size changes latencies normalized and error rate dropped to baseline in ~8m. Marking mitigation successful. I'll prepare a short blameless incident summary.
tim_oncall: taking over final wrap. I'm going to keep the route override and batch caps for 1 hour, then gradually revert. Leaving alerts at reduced sensitivity for 30m.
jen: thanks everyone. action items: (1) INFRA-4521 triage driver leak, (2) ENG-RUNTIME-987 add throttles to continuous-batcher when queue > 10k, (3) postmortem and customer comms draft.
ashok: thanks team, handoff complete. :white_check_mark:
